rules.name: invalid-request-status
rules.reason: Spec divergence, HTTP errors: Java answers a bad sync query or a validation failure with 500 (the query service then returns 502); Rust returns 400 with a text message.

rules.name: unknown-async-id-status
rules.reason: Spec divergence, HTTP errors: Java answers an unknown async result id with a NullPointerException 500; Rust returns 404.

rules.name: invalid-request-empty-200
rules.reason: Spec divergence, HTTP errors: Java answers a FILTER with neither values nor a range, an empty subquery, or non-empty genomicFilters with 200 and an empty body; Rust returns 400 with a text message. The rule covers only these entries and only when the 200 side's body is empty.

rules.name: unknown-async-id-status-empty-200
rules.reason: Spec divergence, HTTP errors: Java answers /status for an unknown async id with 200 and an empty body; Rust returns 404.

rules.name: observation-cross-count-defect
rules.reason: Java OBSERVATION_CROSS_COUNT defect: with two or more selects it can drop keys or hang. Accepted when one side's key set is a strict subset of the other's and every shared key matches, or when a side times out.

rules.name: search-max-double-min-value
rules.reason: Spec divergence, LowRAMLoadingStore.complete and LoadingStore initialize max to Double.MIN_VALUE, so a numeric concept with no value above zero reports a max of 4.9E-324; /search returns that stored max, where Rust returns the real one. Accepted only when every other field of the search body is equal and the real max is zero or below.

rules.name: range-min-above-every-value-empty-200
rules.reason: Spec divergence, Range filters: Java's seekForMinIndex throws when min is above every value (on the harmonization branch, every value of any one selected partition holding the concept), and copyOfRange throws when max is below min; Java then answers 200 with an empty body, where Rust answers 200 with the result for an empty cohort. Accepted only for sync entries whose phenotypic clause holds a FILTER with a min, and only when the empty 200 body is Java's (the run must name its Java side with --java and --java-branch) and Rust's 200 has a body. A string min counts when Jackson coerces it to a number ("NaN" is above every value), and an entry sent as a raw body is read from that body.

rules.name: missing-consents-sync-empty-200
rules.reason: Decision 7 (plan-v2.md) and README, Differences from Java: 'With HPDS_REQUIRE_AUTHORIZATION_FILTER true, a query with no consent value is a 400 "User consents are required for this query" on both query routes. Java answers /query/sync 200 with an empty body and no queryMetadata header'. Accepted only when the entry's query carries no userConsents value, the 400 body is exactly that message (which Rust sends only with the flag on), and the 200 side's body is empty. A 400 for any other reason, such as values on a numeric concept on an unpartitioned store, does not match.

rules.name: missing-consents-async-error
rules.reason: Decision 7 (plan-v2.md) and README, Differences from Java: with the flag on and no consent value Rust refuses POST /query with 400 "User consents are required for this query", where Java answers 'POST /query 200 with a status of ERROR'. Accepted only when the entry's query carries no userConsents value and the refused submit's body is exactly that message, so a sync type submitted on the async route or any other refusal does not match.

rules.name: search-category-values-order
rules.reason: Decision 9 (plan-v2.md) and README, Differences from Java: '/search writes concepts in path order and categoryValues sorted. Java's order of both is unspecified'. Accepted only when sorting every categoryValues array makes the bodies equal.

rules.name: search-concept-order
rules.reason: README, Differences from Java: '/search writes concepts in path order ... Java's order of both is unspecified (an immutable map whose order changes with every start, a HashMap, a HashSet)'. Applies to the null-term answer, an array of one-entry objects. Accepted only when sorting those arrays by path makes the bodies equal.

rules.name: search-concept-and-category-values-order
rules.reason: README, Differences from Java: '/search writes concepts in path order and categoryValues sorted. Java's order of both is unspecified'. For the null-term answer both orders differ at once. Accepted only when sorting the concept array by path and every categoryValues array makes the bodies equal.

rules.name: search-order-and-double-min-value
rules.reason: README, Differences from Java ('/search writes concepts in path order and categoryValues sorted') together with the Spec divergence that LoadingStore starts max at Double.MIN_VALUE, which CSVLoader also uses per partition (harmonization-delta.md section 1, 'The Double.MIN_VALUE max quirk ... apply per partition'). Accepted only when the three normalizations together make the bodies equal.

rules.name: dataframe-tie-order-across-partitions
rules.reason: Decision 4 (plan-v2.md): 'Exports and per-value cross counts merge per-partition by_key data with a k-way merge on patient, with a fixed tie order (partition name order). Java's order across partitions is unspecified, so the order is whitelisted.' A patient in several partitions gets the same values in a cell in another order. Accepted only when sorting the tab-separated values inside every cell makes the exports equal.

rules.name: range-min-above-partition-values-async-error
rules.reason: Spec divergence, Range filters ('Java's seekForMinIndex throws when min is above every value'), which on the harmonization branch applies per partition: a min above every value of one selected partition holding the concept throws, so the Java async query ends in ERROR where Rust answers the cohort. Accepted only for entries whose phenotypic clause holds a FILTER with a min.

rules.name: duplicate-key-last-wins
rules.reason: README, Differences from Java: 'Request bodies holding the same key twice in any object, the envelope, the query, a clause or a userConsents entry included ... are a 400. Jackson keeps the last copy.' Accepted only for the duplicate-key entries.

rules.name: values-on-numeric-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: a FILTER with values on a numeric concept makes PhenoCube.getKeysForValue throw a ClassCastException (PhenoCube.java:54-55), so Java answers /query/sync 200 with an empty body and ends POST /query in ERROR. Rust refuses the query with 400 "<path> is not a categorical variable". Accepted only for that message against Java's empty 200 or async ERROR.

rules.name: range-on-categorical-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: a FILTER with min or max on a categorical concept casts the cube's values to Double and throws (PhenoCube.java:100-103), so Java answers /query/sync 200 with an empty body and ends POST /query in ERROR. Rust refuses the query with 400 "<path> is not a numeric variable". Accepted only for that message against Java's empty 200 or async ERROR.

rules.name: sync-type-on-async-route
rules.reason: README, Differences from Java: 'POST /query accepts only PATIENTS, DATAFRAME, DATAFRAME_TIMESERIES and DATAFRAME_PFB'. Java accepts a sync result type there and then fails it. COUNT, CATEGORICAL_CROSS_COUNT and CONTINUOUS_CROSS_COUNT are queued and end in ERROR (CountV3Processor.java:211 throws UnsupportedOperationException on the worker). CROSS_COUNT and OBSERVATION_CROSS_COUNT make initializeResult throw RuntimeException("UNSUPPORTED RESULT TYPE") (QueryV3Service.java:122), outside the IllegalArgumentException catch; on both Java images the submit still answers 200 with an empty body and no status (checked against main 7798b1c84 and feature-harmonization ecf5a5315). Rust refuses the submit with 400 "Result type <type> is computed synchronously. Submit it with POST /query/sync.". Accepted only for async entries with that exact message for the entry's result type, against a submit Java accepted with 200.

rules.name: genomic-type-on-sync-route
rules.reason: Spec, phenotype-only scope: genomic result types are out of scope. Java answers some of them on /query/sync with 200 and a text such as "VARIANT_LIST query type not allowed"; Rust answers 400 "result type <type> is not supported by this phenotype-only HPDS". Accepted only for sync entries with that exact message for the entry's result type, against a Java 200.

rules.name: variant-spec-path-status
rules.reason: Spec, phenotype-only scope: a concept path shaped like a variant spec (an rs number or chromosome,position,ref,alt) names genomic data. Java looks it up as a phenotype concept, finds none, and answers as for an unknown path (a count of 0, an empty cross count, an export with no rows). Rust refuses it with 400 "variant-spec concept path \"<path>\" is not supported by this phenotype-only HPDS". Accepted only for that message against a Java answer (a sync 200 or an accepted async submit).

rules.name: request-limit-status
rules.reason: README, the HPDS_MAX_* settings: Rust bounds the shape of every query (HPDS_MAX_SELECT_PATHS 5,000 selects, HPDS_MAX_CLAUSE_DEPTH 64 levels, HPDS_MAX_CLAUSE_NODES 10,000 clauses, HPDS_MAX_QUERY_CONCEPTS 20,000 touched concepts), and its JSON reader refuses bodies nested past serde_json's recursion limit of 128, about 63 nested subqueries. Java has no such bounds and answers. Accepted only for a 400 naming one of those four limits or "recursion limit exceeded" against a Java answer (a sync 200 or an accepted async submit). HPDS_MAX_CROSS_COUNT_ENTRIES, which refuses a valid cross count for the size of its answer rather than the shape of the query, is not covered and stays a reported difference.

rules.name: search-shape-main
rules.reason: Contract, main branch only (javaBranch): Rust serves the consent branch's /search shape, SummaryColumnMeta (name, widthInBytes, categorical, categoryValues, min, max, patientCount, timestampMin, timestampMax, nulls written). The original Java HPDS on main serves ColumnMeta (name, categorical, categoryValues for categorical concepts, min and max for numeric ones, observationCount, patientCount). Accepted only when the bodies are equal once every column meta keeps the shared fields (name, categorical, a non-empty categoryValues, a non-null min and max, patientCount) and, as the main loader also starts max at Double.MIN_VALUE (LoadingStore.java:54), a max of 4.9E-324 against a real max of zero or below takes the real value.

rules.name: authorization-filters-main
rules.reason: Contract, main branch only (javaBranch): Rust, like the consent branch, never applies authorizationFilters (the consent branch only validates them, QueryValidator.java:49), while the original Java HPDS on main ANDs each one into the query (PhenotypicQueryExecutor.java:35), so main answers fewer patients. Rust must not replace a main-branch HPDS that relies on authorizationFilters (README, Differences from Java). Accepted only against main, only when the entry's query carries a non-empty authorizationFilters list, both sides answered (sync 200, or async SUCCESS), and main's answer is the narrower one: a COUNT no greater than Rust's, a cross count with the same concepts at the top level and every count under them no greater, a PATIENTS or DATAFRAME export with the same header and a subset of Rust's rows. Against the consent branch, which ignores the filters as Rust does, any difference stays reported.

rules.name: number-too-long-status
rules.reason: Jackson error, invalid input: Jackson 2.21 refuses a number token with more than 1,000 digits (StreamReadConstraints.getMaxNumberLength, counting integer, fraction and exponent digits). Java answers 400 with Spring's JSON error body when the token is in the request body, and 500 with an empty body when it is in a query sent as a JSON string (PicSureV3Service.convertIncomingQuery). Rust refuses the same tokens with 400 and Jackson's text, "Number value length (<n>) exceeds the maximum allowed (1000, from `StreamReadConstraints.getMaxNumberLength()`)". Two 400s already compare equal, so the rule accepts only that message against a Java 500.

rules.name: string-bound-refused-status
rules.reason: Jackson error, invalid input: a min or max sent as a JSON string that Jackson 2.21's double coercion refuses as malformed ("1d", "1f", "0x1p3", "1_000", "-NaN", "1.e5") makes the Java query fail in convertIncomingQuery, which answers 500 with an empty body; Rust refuses it with 400 "invalid value: string <text>, expected a number, a numeric string, or null". Accepted only when the entry's query holds such a string bound (checked with hpds_query::jackson_string_double), the Java side's 500 has an empty body, and the 400 names that string. Strings refused only for their length are number-too-long-status. Holds on both Java branches, which answer alike.

rules.name: filter-without-criteria-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: a FILTER with neither values nor a min or max (a blank string bound counts as none, since Jackson coerces it to null) makes PhenotypicQueryExecutor throw (PhenotypicQueryExecutor.java:90), so Java answers /query/sync 200 with an empty body and ends POST /query in ERROR; Rust refuses it with 400 "Either values or one of min/max must be set for a filter on <path>". invalid-request-empty-200 covers hpds-bench's own error entry for this; this rule covers any entry whose query holds such a filter, and only with that exact refusal against Java's empty 200 or async ERROR.
